title: Thomas Tompion's year-going longcase clock for King William III (RCIN 57800)

subject.summary: Thomas Tompion's year-going equation longcase clock in a burr-walnut case, made for King William III about 1695, now in the Royal Collection (RCIN 57800): a sliding hood with a break-arch pediment, a 24-hour dial, and a glazed lenticle over the pendulum bob.

how: A longcase clock stands on its plinth; the trunk door and the glazed hood door open on hinges.
The hood is a sliding hood: in the clock it lifts up and off; here its glazed door swings.
Behind the dial, three brass plates carry the going train of a year-going timepiece.
The driving weight hangs at the back of the trunk; the pendulum swings behind the dial.
Its bob shows through the arched lenticle glazed low in the trunk door.
The dial is a 24-hour dial; the ring outside it is marked 'Apparant Time'.
The arch above the dial has apertures for the zodiac signs and the sun's place in the ecliptic.
Sizes read from photographs are marked inferred; the overall size is the Trust's measurement.

authoring.provenance_note: Overall size, materials, the year-going equation movement, the 24-hour dial with its Apparant Time circle, the glazed hood door, the brass ball finial, the lenticle and the William III provenance are the Royal Collection Trust's record (RCIN 57800); the inner levels, movement layout, pendulum and weight are read from its two photographs or inferred from Tompion's practice and marked so.
